title: Given two arrays representing the preorder and inorder traversal of a binary tree with unique values, reconstruct and return the original tree.
shortTitle: Construct Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
keyPoints: Preorder gives the next root (first element); inorder splits it into left and right subtrees
A HashMap from value to inorder index makes root lookup O(1) instead of O(n) per node
A single forward-moving pointer into the preorder array supplies each root in order
You must build the left subtree before the right to consume preorder values correctly
Time is O(n) with the map; without it, linear scans make the algorithm O(n^2)
This reconstruction requires unique values; duplicates make the inorder split ambiguous

s1_definition.oneliner: Preorder gives the next root, inorder splits that root into left and right subtrees, and recursion rebuilds the whole tree.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Preorder** visits node, left, right, so the first element is always the root of the current subtree.
- **Inorder** visits left, node, right, so the root's position splits the array into left and right subtree values.
- **HashMap** maps each value to its inorder index for O(1) root lookup.
- **Preorder pointer** moves forward, supplying each root in exactly the order needed.
- **Build order** requires left subtree first, then right, to match preorder's node-left-right sequence.
- **Time** is O(n) with the map; **space** is O(n) for the map and recursion.
s1_definition.analogy: Rajesh has two records of the National Bank of India's org chart taken in two different reading orders. The preorder record always lists a manager before their teams, so the very first name is the top manager. The inorder record lists the left team, then the manager, then the right team. Once Rajesh finds that top manager's name in the inorder record, everyone to the left is the left team and everyone to the right is the right team. He repeats this for each team to rebuild the whole chart.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Reconstruction from preorder and inorder
  ==========================================

  Preorder: [3, 9, 20, 15, 7]    (read left-to-right)
             ^  pointer moves →

  Inorder:  [9, 3, 15, 20, 7]
                 ^
  Step 1: root = 3, split inorder at 3
           left: [9]    right: [15, 20, 7]

  Step 2: root = 9 (next preorder), split: [] | 9 | []
           leaf node

  Step 3: root = 20 (next preorder), split at 20
           left: [15]   right: [7]

  Step 4: root = 15, leaf
  Step 5: root = 7, leaf

  Rebuilt tree:
         3
        / \
       9   20
          /  \
         15    7

  Inorder map:  {9:0, 3:1, 15:2, 20:3, 7:4}
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Reconstructing a binary tree from its preorder and inorder traversals rests on two facts that fit together perfectly. Preorder visits node then left then right, so reading preorder from the front always gives the next root. Inorder visits left then node then right, so finding the root in the inorder array splits it cleanly into the left subtree before it and the right subtree after it.

The implementation keeps a single forward-moving pointer into the preorder array to supply each root, and a precomputed HashMap from value to inorder index for O(1) root lookup. You recurse by passing the current inorder range, creating a node from the next preorder value, looking up its split point, and building the left subtree before the right. The order is critical: building left first matches the preorder consumption sequence, and swapping them corrupts the tree.

Without the HashMap, each root lookup is a linear scan and the algorithm degrades to O(n^2). With the map, it is O(n) overall. The algorithm also requires unique values because duplicates make the inorder split ambiguous.

At the National Bank of India, Rajesh used this to migrate an org hierarchy from a legacy system that had exported the structure only as two traversal logs. The service rebuilt the actual tree from the logs and validated the result by re-traversing and comparing, and the HashMap kept the rebuild fast even for large hierarchies with thousands of employees.

Remember one sentence: preorder gives the root, inorder gives the split, the HashMap makes it linear, and you must build left before right.
